video_title: Cypherpunk Owns $500M of Zcash and 18% of Its Hashrate
gist: Cypherpunk Technologies CIO Will McAvoy (Winklevoss Capital) argues AI-driven de-anonymization of Bitcoin is pushing BTC whales into Zcash, and details CYPH's ~$500M ZEC treasury (~2% of supply, target 5%) plus ~18% of hashrate in a mining business earning ~$1,000/MWh vs ~$130 for Bitcoin, constrained by Bitmain being the sole ASIC maker. He frames CYPH as sum-of-parts (~$1B EV, ZEC/mining ~50/50) rather than mNAV, says the team bought the Orchard-bug dip, and floats 10% of BTC (~$10k ZEC) as reasonable. Note: the intro caption says ZEC went '$50 to $150' but the host later states $50 to ~$1,500.

insights.claim: McAvoy attributes Zcash's run chiefly to AI making transparent ledgers like Bitcoin de-anonymizable: AI can correlate on-chain data with leaked personal data (addresses, SSNs, phone numbers) to identify wallet owners.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Privacy-coin demand is framed as a structural AI-era hedge, not a cyclical narrative.
insights.quote: AI can parse transparent ledger like Bitcoin

insights.claim: The marginal Zcash buyer is mostly large Bitcoin holders who realize Bitcoin's pseudonymity is eroding and that everyone will soon know how much BTC they hold.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Flows from BTC whales into a small-cap asset explain the outsized move; watch whale rotation as a driver.
insights.quote: we are on this path for like everyone to know very soon how much Bitcoin I hold

insights.claim: Leaked personal data is currently 'safe' only because it is too voluminous to exploit manually; AI parsing it alongside wallet data turns it into a targeting tool, so hacks and exploits across the digital economy will increase.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Rising physical/digital security risk for known crypto holders supports demand for shielded assets.
insights.quote: that's true today, but that's just because there's so much data out there that it's like hard to actually use

insights.claim: The host predicts someone will eventually vibe-code a website listing the top 100 Bitcoin holders with names and home addresses, and that spooked whales best explain Zcash's rise; McAvoy agreed '100%'.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: A doxxing event of this kind would be a catalyst for privacy-asset flows.
insights.quote: somebody is going to vibe code a website with the top 100 holders of Bitcoin

insights.claim: McAvoy argues AI breaks 'web2-style privacy in web3' (CoinJoin-type mixing, privacy layers whose data can be subpoenaed or seen), whereas only true ZK-backed self-custodied shielded privacy like Zcash survives.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Competing privacy solutions on transparent chains may be discounted relative to native ZK privacy.
insights.quote: I think AI breaks a lot of these things.

insights.claim: Zcash's multi-year dormancy after ChatGPT is explained by AI's exponential improvement (2023 AI was ~5% as good as today) plus Zcash recently attracting top cryptographers and app teams like Zodl and Visor.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Narrative lag can persist years; capability inflections can trigger re-ratings.

insights.claim: McAvoy cites a chaotic macro backdrop—growing government power, wars, supply-chain disruptions—as attracting non-crypto capital worried about wealth confiscation into Zcash.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Positions ZEC as a geopolitical/confiscation hedge alongside the AI thesis.
insights.quote: in a world of high chaos, um Zcash is just a great asset to own

insights.claim: Zcash mining earns about $1,000 per megawatt-hour versus roughly $130/MWh for Bitcoin mining and about $240/MWh for AI/HPC colocation.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: ZEC mining is ~4x more profitable per MWh than the AI-colocation pivot Bitcoin miners made.
insights.quote: it's earning about $1,000 per megawatt hour

insights.claim: Bitmain is the only manufacturer of Zcash mining equipment, likely producing only low thousands of units per month, and a new order today would take roughly 7-8 months or more to plug in.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Inelastic hardware supply protects incumbent hashrate holders' margins.
insights.quote: There's only one uh manufacturer of Zcash mining equipment. It's Bitmain.

insights.claim: Bitmain is unlikely to shift TSMC allocation from Bitcoin to Zcash machines because Zcash is a small business for it and Bitcoin machine demand remains vast even at thin margins.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Equipment bottleneck should persist; a rising BTC price worsens it.

insights.claim: New Zcash ASIC entrants face costly semiconductor design and must compete for TSMC/Samsung fab capacity against the best-capitalized AI companies, so tight supply could last years, not months.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Excess mining profitability is likely durable over a multi-year horizon.
insights.quote: we're talking years. We're not we're not talking months

insights.claim: Over ~13 months ZEC went from about $50 to about $1,500 (30x) while hashrate rose from 7 to 25 GSol/s (~3.5x), implying mining became roughly 8.5x more profitable.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Hashrate lagging price signals an under-supplied mining market.
insights.quote: the ze price has 30xed, hash rate has 3.5xed

insights.claim: McAvoy compares Zcash mining today to Bitcoin mining in 2016-2017, when machine supply was opaque, players few, and BTC mining earned $300-400/MWh; Zcash now earns over double that.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Analog suggests an early, high-margin phase before industrialization.
insights.quote: it's very similar to mining Bitcoin in 2016 and 2017

insights.claim: About 4 million ZEC (~20% of the 21M cap) remain to be mined, versus ~1 million BTC, since Zcash's identical schedule started in 2016 vs Bitcoin's 2009.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Large remaining emissions make hashrate share a meaningful accumulation channel.

insights.claim: Unlike other Zcash miners that have sold much of their output, Cypherpunk has held all mined ZEC and intends to keep doing so.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Reduces miner sell pressure relative to peers; competitors are net sellers.
insights.quote: so far we've held all of the Zcash we've mined

insights.claim: Cypherpunk Technologies holds about 325,000-330,000 ZEC (just under $500M) and runs the largest Zcash mining operation with roughly 18% of network hashrate.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Core balance sheet and operating facts for CYPH.
insights.quote: We hold about $500 million of Zcash

insights.claim: Including warrants, CYPH trades at about a $1B enterprise value, implying the market values the mining business around $500M with ZEC holdings and mining split roughly 50/50.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Sum-of-parts: any privacy venture portfolio is ascribed ~zero value today.
insights.quote: Zcash and then mining probably 5050

insights.claim: McAvoy says mNAV no longer makes sense for CYPH; analysts should use sum-of-the-parts because the mining business adds substantial value beyond the treasury.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Don't screen CYPH as a DAT premium/discount-to-NAV play.
insights.quote: I don't think MNAP makes any sense anymore

insights.claim: Cypherpunk aims to defend 18-20% of Zcash hashrate (no new miner orders announced), targeting 18-20% of future emissions minus the dev/community-grant cut.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Implies steady ZEC accumulation from ~4M remaining supply, net of dev fund.
insights.quote: we feel really good at being around like the 18 to 20% number

insights.claim: Cypherpunk aims to own 5% of ZEC supply and is currently just under 2%.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Significant future buying (via raises and mining) still ahead.
insights.quote: Uh just under 2%.

insights.claim: CYPH is open to continual capital raises to buy ZEC, mining gear, and privacy investments; its first ~$60M outside raise was deployed into ZEC around when it crossed into triple digits.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Expect ongoing equity issuance; prior raises were highly accretive at low ZEC prices.

insights.claim: CYPH's short-term goal is to be 'alpha to Zcash' via accretive accumulation and profitable mining, and long-term to be the only public-market vehicle for broad privacy-tech exposure over ~5 years.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Positions CYPH vs a Zcash ETF as levered/diversified privacy exposure.
insights.quote: our goal is to be is to be alpha to Zcash

insights.claim: Cypherpunk plans to invest in early-stage privacy startups (e.g., Zodl, the most widely used Zcash wallet), acquire cash-flowing mature businesses, and build in-house across communications, browsing and AI privacy.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Venture/growth bucket is optionality not priced in; wins via exits or ZEC adoption.

insights.claim: McAvoy argues private AI platforms should take payment for inference and tokens in Zcash, positioning ZEC as the base-layer money for private digital life.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Agentic/private AI payments are a potential ZEC demand vector.
insights.quote: paying for inference, paying for tokens in Zcash

insights.claim: The host notes CYPH stock rose about 400% in about 50 days alongside ZEC.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: High beta to ZEC; also the host discloses it is one of his largest equity holdings.

insights.claim: A potential Orchard shielded-pool bug that could have minted unlimited ZEC was found within hours by a Zcash security researcher using a developer version of Opus 4.8 on its release day; ZEC fell from about $600 to $300.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Frontier AI models are now discovering critical crypto vulnerabilities quickly—a recurring tail risk and also a defense.
insights.quote: had a developer version of Opus 4.8. the day Opus 4.8 was released

insights.claim: Cypherpunk judged exploitation exponentially unlikely because the bug went undiscovered for years, a fast patch shipped, and pre-disclosure price action showed no sign of someone minting and dumping ZEC—so it bought the dip.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Use price action and attacker incentives (sell before others find it) to assess hidden inflation risk.
insights.quote: it was going to be a buying opportunity

insights.claim: McAvoy says the most under-discussed part of the Zcash story is its world-class, ideologically aligned team shipping at breakneck pace, naming Dave at Valor, Shawn Bo at Tachyon, the Zodl team and Visor wallet builders.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Developer quality is the key diligence variable he uses, like a VC-backed company.
insights.quote: the biggest part of the story that no one's talking about is the team

insights.claim: Cypherpunk sees Zcash reaching 10% of Bitcoin's market cap—roughly a $10,000 ZEC price—as reasonable and an intermediate-term check-in, not a sell target.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Implies ~6-7x upside from ~$1,500 per the company's framing.
insights.quote: 10% of bitcoin seems like fairly reasonable

insights.claim: Larger TAMs for Zcash are gold and the tens of trillions in offshore wealth and private stores of value like art.
insights.speaker: Will McAvoy (CIO, Cypherpunk Technologies)
insights.so_what: Frames ZEC as a digital private store of value competing with gold/offshore wealth.

insights.claim: The host flags that Lazarus Group appears to be moving funds in and out of the shielded Zcash pool, calling it both a quality signal and a regulatory threat.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Illicit-use headlines are a key regulatory overhang for ZEC.

insights.claim: The host argues Zcash will not be absorbed by nation-states as easily as Bitcoin, as capital controls rise in the West and China cracks down; McAvoy concedes China is a much bigger risk but is optimistic about the US given privacy's role in the Bill of Rights.
insights.speaker: Host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Jurisdictional divergence: US policy is the key swing factor for ZEC.
insights.quote: both superpowers are going to be extremely offended by Zcash
